episodes.workflow: In-rack sprinkler design release and field readiness
episodes.expectedState: Exotec-accepted fitment and design constraints are resolved before fabrication, release, or field dependence.
episodes.firstBreakdown: Field work and released design were already dependent on a configuration Exotec said could not fit the racks.
episodes.trigger: Exotec reviewed the installed/released configuration against rack constraints.
contributingConditions: Acceptance criteria were not closed before downstream commitment
Related McLane design lessons were not converted into a release gate

impacts.method: Source confirms redesign work; hours are not yet measured.
No source-backed cost value has been reconciled.

episodes.earliestSignal: The earlier McLane thread documented the rear-upright and support-elevation constraints before the Superior breakdown surfaced.
episodes.resolution: Open: rebuild the design against the named Exotec standard and close all fitment comments.

evidence.note: Corrected Superior mailbox copy; the false Uniqlo episode is not used.

review.notes: Occurrence is confirmed; financial and schedule burden remain unquantified.

episodes.expectedState: Vendor constraints are resolved and accepted before field installation details are finalized.
episodes.firstBreakdown: Support elevation and allowable upright locations required clarification.
episodes.trigger: The design team surfaced the rear-upright-only constraint and bending-moment concern.
contributingConditions: Equipment geometry constrained usable support locations
consequences: Clarification was closed with an accepted configuration
No schedule impact was stated in the source chain

impacts.method: No schedule impact is stated; this is not proof of zero internal effort.

episodes.earliestSignal: Support elevation and nine-millimeter upright-hole constraints were raised before final installation acceptance.
episodes.resolution: Alleato and Exotec accepted the standard rear-upright vertical support and bracket orientation.

evidence.note: Consistently attributed McLane source showing accepted rear-upright configuration.

review.notes: Retained to learn which early clarification controls distinguish resolution from downstream rework.

episodes.expectedState: Client decisions, prerequisite work, and startup direction are closed before trade mobilization.
episodes.firstBreakdown: ACCO pulled manpower and later did not mobilize because direction and owner decisions remained unresolved.
episodes.trigger: Unresolved duct-sock/startup direction reached the planned work window.
contributingConditions: Decision ownership remained external at the mobilization boundary
Communication handoff was changing during active startup coordination
consequences: Stop-work direction pending an Ulta decision

impacts.method: Sources confirm startup risk and a missed mobilization; exact delay duration is not reconciled.
Remobilization or idle-cost amount is not source-backed yet.

episodes.earliestSignal: ACCO had already pulled manpower pending direction before the missed mobilization was reported.
episodes.resolution: Partially recovered when ACCO agreed to prepare the plenum; later stop-work messaging shows the decision path was not fully closed.

evidence.note: Email documents manpower pullback and recovery attempt around AC-1 startup.
Teams source explicitly records the missed mobilization and stop-work instruction; it is unassigned and therefore cannot independently prove project identity.

review.notes: Cross-source occurrence is strong; exact remobilization cost and final delay remain unknown.

episodes.workflow: Sprinkler material readiness and forward planning
episodes.expectedState: Material constraints are tied to a written look-ahead schedule with required-on-site dates before crews depend on them.
episodes.firstBreakdown: The huddle identified backordered K16 heads and a need to source roughly 900 scarce U-bolts while GPC was already described as delayed.
episodes.trigger: Near-term branch-line work encountered unresolved material availability.
contributingConditions: Written schedules were still being requested
Supplier scarcity and backorder status were active
consequences: Emergency local sourcing and overnight logistics

impacts.method: Source assigns emergency procurement and coordination work; effort hours are unknown.
Meeting states GPC is delayed but does not isolate material-attributable days.

episodes.earliestSignal: Written schedule and material availability were both unresolved before the emergency sourcing action was assigned.
episodes.resolution: Open: confirm K16 shipment timing, allocate available K22 heads, and source U-bolts locally or by courier.

evidence.note: Fireflies morning huddle contains the material quantities, backorder, schedule request, and GPC delay statements.

review.notes: Project 90 is the canonical source attribution, but the episode remains company-level until a canonical GPC project mapping is proven.
